task_summary: Debug production incident: race condition in task scheduler. Identify root cause, evaluate candidate fixes, and plan schema migration under backward-compatibility constraint.

task_graph.root_task: Resolve race condition in task scheduler causing intermittent task duplication in production.

subtasks.description: Identify root cause of task duplication
subtasks.outcome: Race condition in task dispatch: two workers can claim the same task if the claim operation is not atomic against the pending queue.
Three candidates evaluated. Two ruled out (locking semantics, distributed consensus overhead). One preferred (atomic claim via compare-and-swap).

subtasks.description: Plan schema migration for the preferred fix
subtasks.current_focus: Designing backward-compatible migration across two prior schema versions.

subtasks.description: Verify migration does not touch authentication layer

decision_log.decision: Root cause is a race condition in the task claim operation, not a scheduler logic error.
decision_log.rationale: Reproduction shows task duplication only under concurrent worker load. Single-worker runs do not duplicate. Claim operation is read-then-write, not atomic.
alternatives_considered: Scheduler logic error — ruled out, logic is deterministic under single worker
Network partition causing duplicate dispatch — ruled out, duplicates appear within single datacenter

decision_log.decision: Reject fix candidate A (global locking around claim operation).
decision_log.rationale: Global locking serializes all task claims and reduces throughput by an estimated 40%. Unacceptable for the workload profile.

decision_log.decision: Reject fix candidate B (distributed consensus on every claim).
decision_log.rationale: Consensus round-trip adds 15-30ms latency to every claim. Throughput cost exceeds the failure mode's impact. Overkill for the problem.

decision_log.decision: Adopt fix candidate C (atomic claim via compare-and-swap on the pending queue).
decision_log.rationale: Preserves throughput. Introduces no new coordination layer. Requires a schema change to add a version column, which must be backward compatible.

decision_log.decision: Migration must not modify the authentication layer under any circumstances.
decision_log.rationale: Hard constraint established at session start. Authentication is out of scope and is load-bearing for compliance.

active_context.current_problem: Design backward-compatible schema migration for the atomic-claim fix, without touching the authentication layer.
hypotheses: A nullable version column added to the tasks table will preserve compatibility with v1 and v2 read paths.
v3 write paths need to populate the version column, but v1 and v2 write paths must continue to function during rollout.
A shadow write during the transition window may be required to backfill the version column without downtime.
active_context.last_action: Drafted the v3-to-v2 compatibility path. Not yet validated against v1.
next_steps: Validate migration against v1 read/write paths
Verify no authentication table is touched by the migration
Draft rollback procedure for the case where the migration must be reversed
constraints: Must preserve compatibility with schema v1 and v2
Must not modify the authentication layer
Rollback must be possible within 15 minutes

critical_excerpts.annotation: The non-atomic claim operation. Between listPending() and markClaimed(), another worker can claim the same task. This is the exact location of the race condition.

critical_excerpts.content:
CREATE TABLE tasks (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  status TEXT NOT NULL,
  claimed_by TEXT,
  claimed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  payload JSONB NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
critical_excerpts.annotation: Current tasks table. No version column. The migration adds a nullable version column and backfills it via shadow write.

critical_excerpts.content:

);
critical_excerpts.annotation: v1 tasks table. No claimed_at, no version. Backward compatibility requires that v1 write paths continue to function without modification, which is why the version column must be nullable with a default.
